journal_name: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics

abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-modal representation learning framework for heterogeneous biomedical data integration, addressing a fundamental challenge in health informatics where diverse data modalities remain siloed. Existing approaches typically handle each data type independently, failing to capture complex cross-modal relationships essential for comprehensive patient assessment. We propose the Hierarchical Attention Graph Network (HAGN), which constructs dynamic interconnections among clinical notes, laboratory results, imaging data, and wearable sensor streams through learnable attention mechanisms. Theoretically, we establish convergence guarantees for the proposed heterogeneous feature alignment objective and prove that HAGN achieves lower bound optimization for multi-modal representation disentanglement. Our mathematical analysis reveals that the framework's performance scales logarithmically with modality diversity, providing theoretical justification for its applicability in large-scale medical data environments. Experiments conducted on MIMIC-IV and UK Biobank datasets demonstrate that HAGN outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 12.4% in disease prediction accuracy and 18.7% in patient clustering coherence. This paradigm shift from modality-specific to unified heterogeneous representation offers a foundational advancement for personalized medicine applications.

Electronic health records contain rich temporal information that existing clinical decision support systems inadequately exploit due to limitations in modeling long-term dependencies. This paper presents an enhanced temporal reasoning framework that significantly advances the state-of-the-art in EHR-based diagnosis prediction. Our approach, Temporal-Enhanced Knowledge Transformer (TEKT), integrates structural medical knowledge graphs with transformer architectures through a novel time-aware attention mechanism. We introduce the Clinical Evolution Loss function, which explicitly models disease progression trajectories and treatment response patterns. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that TEKT achieves O(log n) computational complexity while maintaining O(n) receptive field for temporal dependencies, a substantial improvement over existing recurrent approaches. Extensive validation on three large-scale EHR datasets shows relative improvements of 15.2% in macro F1-score and 22.8% in early diagnosis accuracy compared to previous best methods. The framework enables interpretable clinical insights through attention weight visualization, supporting physician decision-making in patient monitoring scenarios. This work significantly advances medical data analysis capabilities while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for clinical deployment.

This paper presents a novel edge-computing architecture for real-time physiological signal processing in wearable health devices, fundamentally reimagining how continuous patient monitoring systems handle latency and privacy constraints. Current cloud-centric approaches introduce unacceptable delays for critical health alerts and compromise patient data confidentiality through external transmission. Our EdgeMed framework deploys lightweight neural networks directly on wearable hardware, enabling immediate physiological anomaly detection without cloud dependency. The system incorporates a novel adaptive quantization mechanism that dynamically adjusts model precision based on computational budget and signal complexity. We designed a federated aggregation protocol that enables collaborative model improvement across devices while preserving data locality. Implementation on commercial smartwatch platforms demonstrates 94.6% arrhythmia detection accuracy with sub-100ms response latency, consuming only 23mW average power. The architecture supports seamless handoff to cloud resources when processing demands exceed edge capabilities. This paradigm shift toward edge-native health monitoring enables continuous patient surveillance in resource-constrained environments while establishing new standards for healthcare data security.

This paper presents an enhanced telemedicine platform architecture that significantly advances remote patient monitoring capabilities through intelligent triage and adaptive data fusion. Existing telehealth systems suffer from information overload for clinicians and limited predictive capabilities for early intervention. Our TeleHealth Intelligence System (THIS) integrates multi-source patient data streams including vital signs, patient-reported symptoms, and historical medical records through a novel hierarchical fusion engine. We developed a context-aware risk stratification module using recurrent attention networks that achieves 89.3% accuracy in predicting patient deterioration within 6 hours. The system incorporates a conversational AI interface for natural patient interaction and automated health education delivery. Deployment across three hospital networks comprising 15,000+ patients demonstrated 34% reduction in unnecessary emergency transfers, 28% improvement in chronic disease management adherence, and 41% decrease in clinician response time to critical alerts. The platform maintains HIPAA compliance through advanced encryption and audit mechanisms while supporting interoperability with existing electronic health record systems. This substantial improvement in telemedicine infrastructure addresses critical gaps in accessible healthcare delivery.
